transcript:
HEADER: 2026-03-31 14:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Claire (Redwood CSM), Maya (ACME Head of Platform), Luis (ACME SRE), Priya (ACME CISO), Diego (ACME Eng Mgr)

AUTOGEN SUMMARY: Follow-up on ACME outage on 2026-03-22; review RCA, mitigations, SLA impact, and next steps. Action items captured.

TOPICS: RCA overview; root cause (autoscaler bug + cache eviction interplay); temporary mitigations applied (rollback, rate-limiting); long-term fixes (autoscaling patch, KV-cache persistence, better alerting); security/compliance checks.

TRANSCRIPT:
00:00 Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know time is tight. We'll kick off quick. So this is the postmortem follow-up from the 03-22 outage at ACME, Samir is going to run through the tech RCA and then we'll cover mitigations and next steps.
00:14 Maya (ACME): Thanks Jordan. Wanted to be clear up front, the priority is residual risk — we had customer-facing timeouts and that impacted two payment flows. We need concrete mitigations and timeline.
00:28 Samir (SE): Yep. Quick recap: on 03-22 at ~02:12 UTC we saw an abnormal spike in request concurrency to the Redwood Dedicated pool serving your models. Autoscaler hit a bug where scale-grace was set incorrectly, causing underprovisioning during surge. At the same time prefix KV cache evicted more aggressively due to a mempressure signal from the runtime; resulting in cache churn and heavier kernel work, we got CPU/GPU scheduling pressure, queuing, and elevated tail latency, then retries from the application blew up connection counts.
00:52 Luis (SRE): Just to pause — you said mempressure triggered eviction — were those eviction thresholds tuned by us or defaults? The behavior was surprising to us.
01:01 Samir (SE): It was defaults. We tested with your traffic shape in staging but didn't hit the same seq-len distribution; the production seq lengths were longer and kept KV sets live longer which combined with a GC hiccup in the runtime. Also note that one of the autoscaler heuristics mis-evaluated the steady-state due to a metrics namespace mismatch, so scaling lagged.
01:20 Maya: OK, that matches what we saw. We also noticed a weird interaction where the fallback to region-b failover didn't trigger fast enough.
01:28 Claire (CSM): Right, we allowed cross-region fallback but the policy was too conservative for this workload.
01:33 Priya (CISO): From security perspective we need the audit logs for that window and confirmation whether any customer PII touched logs or was retained.
01:42 Jordan: We'll include that in the postmortem doc. Claire, can you take point on audit logs?
01:47 Claire: Yup, I'll pull and share.
01:50 Samir: Moving on to the root cause timeline — 02:10 UTC queue started backing up, 02:17 we started dropping requests at the edge, 02:25 our internal mitigation (rollback of a recent kernel optimization) was applied, 02:35 we opened a hotfix to autoscaler config, 02:50 region fallback engaged but lagged, and by 03:05 traffic normalized.
02:12 Diego (ACME): When you say rollback of kernel optimization — was that a model-level or runtime patch? We saw different model latencies after.
02:20 Samir: It was a runtime fix — a recent kernel scheduling tweak that we had rolled out to reduce tail lat for some model shapes; in your case it changed the memory/kcache eviction timing. We rolled that back to the previous kernel line which stabilized resource usage. The model output didn't change, but latencies returned to baseline.
02:36 Luis: Is there a permanent fix? We can't keep rolling back prod changes.
02:40 Samir: Absolutely. Short term: we've got a patch to the autoscaler to fix the metrics namespace mismatch and we're proposing to increase the scale headroom for your pool by 20% during heavy batch windows. Medium term: persist a portion of KV cache to local SSD to reduce churn on mempressure, add a conservative cache-priming policy for long-seq sessions. Long term: some of this will be addressed by better kernel selection heuristics and improved simulator workload testing.
03:05 Maya: Sounds reasonable. What about SLO impact and credits? We track a 99.9 latency SLO, this was a longer tail outage.
03:13 Jordan: We'll calculate exact SLO breaches and apply credits per contract. Claire will follow up on the credit calculation and timeline.
03:20 Priya: Also need to understand whether logs containing tokens or PII were accessible to Redwood engineers during the incident.
03:27 Jordan: No access to PII was performed; we only saw telemetry and server error traces. We'll provide the log export and a brief memo on access controls.
03:35 Claire: I'll share the SOC2 evidence binder and current RBAC settings for the incident period.
03:40 Diego: Can you summarize the mitigation plan and rollout schedule? We need to coordinate change windows.
03:46 Samir: Proposed plan:
- Week 1 (this week): Patch autoscaler and increase headroom on your dedicated pool; add emergency rate-limiting at the edge to prevent retry storms (hotfix).
- Week 2: Deploy KV-cache persistence prototype to a canary subset (10% of nodes) in a non-prod mirror, run replay test with your 03-22 traffic; measure tail latency and eviction rates.
- Week 3: If canary looks good, roll to 50% with canary traffic, then full rollout with a rollback playbook.
- Parallel: Improve alerting thresholds and add a new SRE runbook for this specific failure mode (autoscaler + KV eviction).
04:19 Luis: For the replay test, we need the fixture — we'll provide logs but will Redwood need any synthetic traffic harness?
04:27 Samir: We have a replay harness; we'll need the exported request traces. Also we'll create a small script to anonymize any tokens.
04:35 Maya: We also need a runbook review with our on-call rotation. Can we schedule a 60m workshop?
04:42 Jordan: Yes, we'll schedule the runbook workshop week of Apr 6.
04:48 Priya: On compliance: please include an explanation of why the audit logs were delayed and what changes you'll make to ensure immediate log export for incident windows.
04:56 Claire: We'll include the log export SLA changes in the postmortem and propose a daily ship to your central logging bucket for a 30-day retention as a temporary measure.
05:08 Diego: Any permanent architecture changes? Are we looking at multi-region active-active?
05:13 Samir: Active-active is on the table but it's a heavier lift. Short term we recommend stronger cross-region failover policy and a lighter-weight regional spillover. We'll work with you to quantify cost.
05:25 Maya: Cost is a concern — Megacorp AI pitched a multi-region model host but it's expensive. We prefer a cost-aware solution that meets SLO.
05:34 Jordan: Understood. Redwood Optimize can help quantify trade-offs — Samir will add expected cost delta in the mitigation doc.
05:41 Diego: One more question: were any platform-level keys rotated during the incident? We saw a couple of retries in our KMS logs.
05:49 Claire: No rotations were performed by Redwood during the incident window. Any KMS activity was read-only. We'll confirm and include an audit snippet.
05:58 Luis: Will the proposed KV-cache persistence require downtime?
06:03 Samir: The persistence prototype is rolling and non-blocking; for mainline rollout we'll schedule a small maintenance window (under 15 minutes) for the final migration step, but canary phases are no-downtime.
06:16 Maya: Ok. Let's talk about communications — we need a customer-facing postmortem to share with our execs and a more detailed technical appendix for our SREs.
06:25 Jordan: We'll produce both — A one-pager for execs and a technical appendix with timings, logs, and remediation details.
06:33 Priya: For the technical appendix please redact any tokens and include a section on RBAC and KMS access during the incident.
06:41 Claire: Will do.
06:45 Samir: Quick note on monitoring improvements: we'll add a synthetic probe that mimics your tail token sizes and sequence lengths, and new alerts on cache-eviction-rate and autoscaler-lag. We'll also add a dashboard tile showing prefix-KV hit ratio.
07:03 Diego: Good. Last item: can Redwood propose an SLA change or an enhanced incident runbook as part of an enterprise add-on?
07:12 Jordan: Yes — we can propose a premium SLA or Dedicated support add-on; Jordan: I'll send options and pricing.
07:20 Maya: timeline recap please?
07:22 Jordan: Recap: postmortem doc by 2026-04-02; autoscaler patch + headroom this week; KV-cache replay benchmark by 2026-04-05; runbook workshop wk of 2026-04-06; mitigation rollout schedule by 2026-04-07. Credits calculation and audit log export by 2026-04-03.
07:44 Priya: Thank you.
07:46 Jordan: Any other questions?
07:48 Maya: None. Thanks.
07:50 Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc and action items.
07:56 (call ends)

NOTES: Transcript contains slight ASR errors and occasional mis-parsed product names (e.g., "Redwood dedicate" appears once). References to the "kernel optimization" may be simplified in summary. Links shared: postmortem draft (link), SOC2 evidence binder (link), replay-harness README (link).

END OF TRANSCRIPT.
